answer: In an agent economy, each new identity must lock a scarce, nontransferable reputation bond and earn access through randomly assigned cross-checks: a kernel of peers compares its work, while hidden challenge tasks expose copied behavior. A suspected cluster is quarantined in a canyon and its bond is slashed after proof of collusion. Creating many fake identities therefore requires capital, sustained honest work, and risks losing every account; jade badges add trust only after costly history.
